narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date across 3 awards, with an average award size of $410M and obligations down 5.9% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations show rapid growth since FY22, with FY21 at $67.4M, FY22 at $6.7M, FY23 at $982M, FY24 at $1.4B, FY25 at $1.3B, and FY26 at $1.2B. The Department of Energy is the dominant buyer, obligating $1.2B so far this fiscal year. The largest market is Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences with $1.2B obligated, followed by Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools with $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services with $31.3K. Current-year totals are partial because figures are fiscal year to date. These figures are contract obligations except where a table labels award-value figures as total contract values. The picture is large, concentrated, and tied to a single agency and market.

sections.heading: Who buys from Regents of the University of California?
sections.body: Department of Energy obligated $1.2B from Regents of the University of California in FY2026 to date. Department of Commerce obligated $31.3K. The buyer base is therefore concentrated, with the Department of Energy representing the vast majority of obligations.

sections.heading: What are Regents of the University of California's largest markets and recent trends?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences received $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools received $4M, and Computer Facilities Management Services received $31.3K. Obligations are down 5.9% year over year, and the vendor recorded 3 awards with an average award size of $410M.

faq.q: How much does Regents of the University of California make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California obligated $1.2B from federal contracts in FY2026 to date. The vendor received 3 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $410M. Current-year totals are fiscal year to date and obligations are down 5.9% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Regents of the University of California?
faq.a: Department of Energy and Department of Commerce buy from Regents of the University of California. Department of Energy obligated $1.2B and Department of Commerce obligated $31.3K in FY2026 to date.

faq.q: What does Regents of the University of California sell to the government?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California sells research and development and related services to the government. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences received $1.2B, Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools received $4M, and Computer Facilities Management Services received $31.3K in FY2026 to date.

faq.q: Which Regents of the University of California contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California has current obligations recorded for ongoing contracts, but the FACTS do not list specific expiring-contract entries. The available tables show award counts and total obligations by fiscal year and market rather than an expiring-contract list.
